claims.statement: ChessCore._prepare builds every LLM request as model_view(messages, turns, memory=...) followed by one trailing HumanMessage from ChessCore.turn_message, which renders a PositionView via render_position; the position block is never written to stored messages.

ChessCore.turn_message narrows candidates to those still in allowed_moves before rendering, and the bundled renderer shows the 'Suggested candidates' line only when candidates exist and move_list is 'both' or 'candidates' (also on restricted turns).

When allowed_moves differs from the full legal set (PositionView.restricted), render_position always adds 'Only these moves are permitted' regardless of move_list; the bundled renderer's 'Legal moves' list appears only on unrestricted turns with move_list 'both' or 'legal'.

Position commands open a turn with a stored delta message from delta_text: 'New game. You are <side>.' on a fresh thread, the new movetext since the last turn, or 'Your move as <side>.' when nothing new was played.

memory is a boolean (default False) on create_chess_agent and CoreSettings, with no 'full' mode. With memory off the model view contains only messages from the current turn's opened_message_id onward; with memory on it contains the whole stored conversation minus earlier turns' rejected replies and feedback.

With memory on or off, the current turn shows all its feedback but only its latest rejected reply, reasoning blocks are stripped from all other AI messages, only Human/AI messages pass, and returned messages are deep copies so wrappers cannot mutate state.

create_chess_agent defaults memory to False and, only when memory is True, appends ChessSummarization after core, ForcedMoveMiddleware and all user middleware (only StallRetry follows it), raising ChessContractError 'memory needs a model' if no model is given.

ChessSummarization defaults to trigger ('fraction', 0.7), keep ('messages', 20) and CHESS_SUMMARY_PROMPT, which tells the summarizer to ignore rejected moves and retry feedback and not to list moves or describe the board.

ChessSummarization raises ChessContractError if summary_prompt lacks {messages} or if keep is not ('messages', n) with n >= 2*max_retries+2, so one turn's opening, attempts and feedback can always be kept.

A fractional summarization trigger requires the model profile's max_input_tokens (read by input_limit); without it ChessSummarization raises ChessContractError advising a profile, a summarization middleware with an absolute trigger, or turning memory off.

A preconfigured SummarizationMiddleware passed as summarization= is converted with ChessSummarization.from_middleware, copying trigger, keep, summary_prompt, trim_tokens_to_summarize and token_counter; the shared build_agent used by the server and CLI never passes summarization=, so deployed games always use the fractional default trigger.

Surfaces build models with one chat_model factory (langchain_chess.chat_models), via build_agent's default_model or the server's server_model; it rejects a reasoning effort for a model known not to take one, sizes the output budget as MAX_TOKENS=64000 capped by the model's output limit and half of a small window (an explicit max_tokens wins, and one filling the window raises ModelArgumentsError); gateway (langsmith:) models get profile max_input_tokens = context_window - budget when the pricing snapshot knows the window (no profile otherwise), and native profiles keep their fields but have max_input_tokens lowered to min(native limit, window - budget).

ChessSummarization runs the stock summarization hook inside a 'summary' recorder sink and provider_errors(), records its provider calls as kind 'summary' on the current turn's calls in the same state update as the message rewrite, and gives the id-less summary HumanMessage an id and marks it consumed so it is never treated as a command.
ChessSummarization reports its name as 'SummarizationMiddleware' so graph node names such as SummarizationMiddleware.before_model stay stable.

memory, move_list, show_fen, show_board and system_prompt are CoreSettings fields inherited by ChessContext on every surface; memory is a strict bool (default False in every settings version), so string values such as 'full' fail validation, and build_agent drops memory when policy is 'systemone' because no model is built.

ChessCore's wrap_model_call runs the handler inside errors.provider_errors(), which re-raises exceptions whose text matches overflow hints (prompt is too long, context length, context_length, maximum context, too many tokens, input is too long) as ContextBudgetError and provider 400s about the reasoning effort as ReasoningEffortError; other errors propagate unchanged and the turn stays pending.
Retry feedback messages list the allowed moves in SAN and, for an empty reply, say the output budget was probably spent on reasoning.

The shared build_agent rejects memory=True with ChessContractError ('no known input limit, so it can't use memory') when the constructed model has no known input limit, unless the policy is systemone (no model, memory dropped).

The server's GET /ui/model route returns max_input_tokens from the cached model_limit(model), which is input_limit(default_model(ChessContext(model=model))) or None if the model can't be built, plus takes_effort; the new-game dialog offers memory only for models with a known input limit.

With fixed_topology=True and memory=False, create_chess_agent appends NoSummarization (named SummarizationMiddleware, with no-op before_model hooks) so the graph has the same nodes for every memory setting; the server always builds with fixed_topology=True, including the settings-free shape() graph used for reads.
A model reply with no text is stored as the placeholder '[no text in reply]' (keeping id and usage), and the resulting retry feedback says the output budget was probably spent on reasoning.
The summarization trigger counts an overhead of the system prompt plus the turn's position message on top of stored messages, but trimming and the keep cutoff count only stored messages.

With memory on, create_chess_agent rejects a system prompt whose token count reaches a summarization trigger threshold (ChessSummarization.check_room), since it would summarize before every call; with memory off a long prompt is accepted.

The bundled position_renderer(show_fen, show_board, move_list) supplies the FEN, ASCII board and move lists; a custom render_position= replaces it, but render_position always keeps core's lines: moves so far, a non-standard starting FEN, side to move, check, permitted moves on restricted turns and the MOVE request.
create_chess_agent rejects an empty system_prompt with ChessContractError; None keeps the bundled SYSTEM_PROMPT.
The UCI engine exposes Memory as a check option that also accepts the legacy values 'summarize' and 'none' as true and false.
